articles.title: Eight Indian Americans Just Won a Fellowship That Pays $90,000 for Being an Immigrant. Here's What They Study.
articles.excerpt: The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships picked 30 scholars from 1,800 applicants. More than a quarter are of Indian origin — a pattern that says something about the community's bet on education.
articles.image_caption: Graduates celebrating at a university commencement ceremony
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans dominate a top immigrant fellowship, reflecting the diaspora's deep investment in education and research — even as the visa system they depend on faces political headwinds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Top Aerospace Body Just Gave Its Highest Honour to India's Moon Mission. The Diaspora Noticed.
articles.excerpt: AIAA's Goddard Astronautics Award — previously reserved for the Hubble and James Webb telescope teams — went to ISRO's Chandrayaan-3. Ambassador Kwatra accepted it in Washington.
articles.image_caption: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander photographed on the lunar surface by the Pragyan rover
articles.nri_angle: The award validates the technical ecosystem that produced hundreds of thousands of Indian-origin aerospace professionals now working in America's own space enterprise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian American Couple Pledged $1 Million to Feed America's Hungry. Their Movement Has Already Delivered 30 Million Meals.
articles.excerpt: The HungerMitao movement channels Indian diaspora resources into America's food banks. India's consul general attended the latest gala — a sign of how seriously New Delhi takes diaspora philanthropy.
articles.image_caption: Volunteers packing food donations at a community food bank
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are redirecting philanthropic energy from remittances to local American communities, building social capital and complicating the narrative that the diaspora only takes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York State Senate Asks Governor to Proclaim August 15 as India Independence Day
articles.excerpt: Resolution J1935 celebrates Indian-American contributions as the diaspora's political footprint in New York deepens
articles.image_caption: The New York State Capitol building in Albany, where the Senate adopted the India Independence Day resolution

sources.label: New York State Senate Legislature Records
Consulate General of India New York

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Graduates Who Go Home See Their Income Multiply 8.4 Times. A New Report Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: India hit a record $135 billion in remittances last year. A 12-year study of 25,000 students shows exactly where that money comes from — and what happens when it flows the other way.
articles.image_caption: An IIT campus in India — a new report finds graduates who return home see income multiply over peers who stay abroad
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Gave Foreign Funds a Tax Holiday on Government Bonds. It Forgot About Its Own Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: A new ordinance exempts FPIs from tax on G-Sec interest and capital gains. Individual NRI investors, who have been asking for parity for years, are once again told to wait — or to find a workaround.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where monetary and investment policy is shaped
articles.nri_angle: NRI retail investors who hold or want to hold Indian government bonds are directly affected. The ordinance creates a two-tier system where institutional foreign money gets tax-free treatment while individual diaspora investors — contributing the same foreign capital — pay up to 20 per cent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Built a Digital Portal to Turn the Diaspora Into a $500 Billion Trade Engine. Here's How It Works.
articles.excerpt: At a gala in New Jersey, India's Consul General in New York unveiled a first-of-its-kind platform connecting Indian exporters directly with American buyers — and laid out the roadmap for 'Mission 500.'
articles.image_caption: The Consulate General of India in New York, which developed the new trade facilitation portal
articles.nri_angle: The portal positions the nearly four million Indian Americans as a 'living bridge' for bilateral trade, offering them a direct role in connecting Indian MSMEs and artisans with US buyers. It also reflects a shift from treating the diaspora as remittance senders to treating them as trade facilitators.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Is Picking Up the Tab on NRI Deposits. Banks Are Already Lining Up.
articles.excerpt: India's central bank will absorb hedging costs on foreign-currency deposits until September, hoping to lure billions from the diaspora as the rupee slides to record lows.
articles.image_caption: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra at a monetary policy announcement in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, Gulf, and Europe could see higher interest rates on their Indian bank deposits as the RBI subsidises hedging costs, making FCNR(B) accounts significantly more attractive during a narrow September window.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Is Now Live in Nine Countries. The Endgame Is Bigger Than Payments.
articles.excerpt: Cambodia and Nepal are the latest additions to India's expanding digital payments network, but the RBI's real ambition — a sovereign digital currency that rewires how $135 billion in diaspora remittances move — is only now coming into focus.
articles.image_caption: A contactless payment using a smartphone and QR code scanner at a retail counter
articles.nri_angle: UPI abroad lets NRIs pay at merchants in 9 countries without cash or international cards. The India-UAE CBDC corridor, once live, could fundamentally reduce the cost and speed of the $20+ billion annual Gulf-India remittance flow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's Caste Bills Are Dead. The Hindu Community That Killed Them Wants to Talk About What Almost Happened.
articles.excerpt: After two years of grassroots lobbying by the Coalition of Hindus of North America, Senate Bill S.6531 and Assembly Bill A.6920 failed to advance — a victory that Hindu advocacy groups say stopped a religiously coded ethnic classification from becoming law.
articles.image_caption: The New York State Capitol in Albany, where caste-related human rights legislation failed to advance
articles.nri_angle: The bills would have added 'caste' as a protected category under New York's Human Rights Law — language that Hindu and Indian-American advocacy groups argued would single out their community for stereotyping and institutional bias. The outcome is the latest chapter in a legislative battle that has played out across California, Seattle, and now New York.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 14-Year-Old From Rancho Cucamonga Just Spelled 32 Words in 90 Seconds. The Scripps Trophy Is His.
articles.excerpt: Shrey Parikh set a new spell-off record to claim the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee title, continuing a decades-long streak of Indian-American dominance at the competition.
articles.image_caption: The Scripps National Spelling Bee stage at DAR Constitution Hall in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American children have won 21 of the last 28 Scripps titles. Five of nine finalists this year were of Indian origin. The Bee has become one of the most visible stages for diaspora academic achievement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Will Let 20,000 H-1B Holders Renew Visas Without Leaving the Country
articles.excerpt: A December pilot program will spare Indian tech professionals the trip back to a consulate abroad. The vast majority of beneficiaries will be Indian nationals.
articles.image_caption: U.S.-India Consular Dialogue delegation at the State Department in Washington, D.C.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Largest Diaspora No Longer Wants to Be Defined by Wire Transfers. It Has a Blueprint Instead.
articles.excerpt: Indiaspora's 'Partners in Progress' report, drawn from 200 leaders across 24 countries, maps how 35 million overseas Indians are shifting from remittance senders to strategic partners in India's rise.
articles.image_caption: Indian Americans — the world's largest diaspora now shaping policy beyond remittances (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora's evolving relationship with India — from one-way remittance flows to two-way investment, technology, and institutional partnerships — and the structural barriers that remain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Doctors Built a Free Clinic in Suburban Chicago. Now It Opens Six Days a Week.
articles.excerpt: The IAMA Charitable Foundation's Seva clinic has added women's health, telehealth, and a near-daily schedule — a quiet expansion that makes it one of the most ambitious diaspora-run health projects in the country.
articles.image_caption: Volunteer healthcare workers at a community clinic — a model Indian American doctors in suburban Chicago have scaled to six days a week (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian American physicians channelling professional success into free healthcare for underserved populations — a direct expression of the immigrant compact that brought many to the U.S. through medicine.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Hundred South Asian Leaders Walked Into the Mayflower Hotel. The Next Day, the President Targeted Them on Social Media.
articles.excerpt: Indian American Impact's 10th anniversary summit in Washington brought Vivek Murthy, four members of Congress, and 21 advocacy groups to Capitol Hill — just as anti-immigrant rhetoric hit a new pitch.
articles.image_caption: Former U.S. Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy, who opened the Impact Summit with a keynote on community care
articles.nri_angle: South Asian Americans organising politically and asserting civic belonging in the face of rising anti-immigrant rhetoric — the core tension of diaspora identity in 2026 America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sunil Gavaskar Auctioned His Cricket Bats for Blind Children. The Diaspora Wrote the Cheques.
articles.excerpt: At back-to-back galas in New Jersey, two Indian American foundations raised nearly $1 million to fight blindness in India — continuing a tradition of diaspora philanthropy that has restored sight to millions.
articles.image_caption: Sunil Gavaskar, cricketing legend and guest of honour at the Sankara Eye Foundation USA gala
articles.nri_angle: These twin galas illustrate the quiet machinery of NRI philanthropy — professionals and entrepreneurs in America funding eye surgeries, training doctors, and building hospitals across India, one fundraiser dinner at a time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Leads the World in Building America's Billion-Dollar Startups. The Numbers Are Not Even Close.
articles.excerpt: A new study finds Indian immigrants have founded 96 US unicorns — more than Israel, the UK and China combined at the top. Six Indians are among 15 immigrants who built two or more billion-dollar companies.
articles.image_caption: Jay Chaudhry, founder of Zscaler and the wealthiest Indian immigrant startup founder in America
articles.nri_angle: The NFAP study quantifies what the diaspora has long sensed: Indian immigrants are not just filling jobs in America but creating the companies that define its economic future, from cybersecurity to AI to aviation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Is Weeks Away from Ruling on Birthright Citizenship. Indian Visa Holders Have the Most at Stake.
articles.excerpt: Trump became the first sitting president to attend oral arguments in April. Six justices pushed back. The ruling, expected by late June, could redefine who counts as American-born.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C., at dusk
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Doubled the Limit for NRI Investors. Then They Tried to Open an Account.
articles.excerpt: The RBI and Finance Ministry just raised how much NRIs can invest in Indian stocks. But a GPS check, an Aadhaar OTP that won't arrive abroad, and two incompatible KYC systems mean most diaspora investors still can't get past the login screen.
articles.image_caption: A smartphone displaying investment charts alongside a passport and US dollars — the reality of NRI investing
articles.nri_angle: For millions of NRIs who want to participate in India's equity markets, the problem is no longer the limit — it is the paperwork. SEBI's geo-tagging requirement, Aadhaar-dependent e-signatures, and incompatible KYC systems between the regulator and GIFT City create a friction tax that specifically penalises the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Chhattisgarh Boy Who Worked Night Shifts at 17 Just Wrote Houston's Largest Hospital Cheque.
articles.excerpt: Brij and Sunita Agarwal's $5.5 million gift to St. Luke's Health-Sugar Land will rename the patient tower and fund a primary care clinic in one of Houston's fastest-growing — and most underserved — suburbs.
articles.image_caption: A medical centre in Sugar Land, Texas, one of Houston's fastest-growing suburbs
articles.nri_angle: The Agarwals' trajectory — from a small town in Chhattisgarh to running 150 restaurants across Texas and writing a record hospital cheque — embodies the Indian-American philanthropy boom that now exceeds $5 billion annually, reshaping the healthcare and education infrastructure of the very suburbs the diaspora has made home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Mother and Son From Haryana Just Became Mayors of Two British Councils. Neither Planned a Career in Politics.
articles.excerpt: Parveen Rani and Tushar Kumar, who moved from Rohtak to Hertfordshire in 2013, were sworn in as mayors of neighbouring councils within a single week — the first mother-son pair to hold simultaneous mayoral offices in UK history.
articles.image_caption: A street in Watford, Hertfordshire — the kind of English town where Indian diaspora families like the Dahiyas are reshaping local civic life (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A Haryana family's civic rise in Britain illustrates how diaspora communities are moving from cultural preservation into political leadership — and redefining what representation looks like in local government.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: It's June and the NRI Tax Clock Is Ticking. Here's Everything That Changed This Year.
articles.excerpt: Budget 2026 scrapped the TAN requirement for property deals, widened reporting thresholds, and opened a six-month amnesty window for undisclosed foreign assets. For the five million NRIs filing Indian returns, the rules have never been more different — or more forgiving.
articles.image_caption: North Block in New Delhi, home to India's Finance Ministry — the building from which NRI tax rules originate (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Every NRI with Indian income, property, or investments must navigate a tax system that changed more in 2026 than in the previous five years combined. The reforms reward compliance and punish ignorance in roughly equal measure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bobby Mukkamala Survived Brain Surgery and Won the AMA Presidency. His Next Fight Is American Healthcare Itself.
articles.excerpt: The first physician of Indian heritage to lead the American Medical Association is a brain tumour survivor from Flint, Michigan — and the unlikely face of a diaspora that now shapes US health policy from the top.
articles.image_caption: AMA President Bobby Mukkamala delivers remarks at a health policy event in Washington, DC
articles.nri_angle: Bobby Mukkamala's AMA presidency represents the structural influence Indian American physicians have built in US healthcare — from free clinics to national policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's Yoga Guru Will Stand at Times Square on June 21. The Diaspora Arranged the Invitation.
articles.excerpt: Padma Shri HR Nagendra will headline the biggest International Day of Yoga celebrations in the US — at the Lincoln Memorial and Times Square. Behind the scenes, a decade-long diaspora network made it happen.
articles.image_caption: Yoga practitioners at Times Square in New York City during International Day of Yoga celebrations
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora organisations in the US have built a decade-long infrastructure to embed yoga in American public life — from the UN to Capitol Hill to Times Square.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five South Asian Candidates Just Won or Advanced in Georgia. One Could Make History.
articles.excerpt: Nabilah Islam Parkes is poised to become the first South Asian and Asian American lieutenant governor nominee in Georgia history. She is not alone — Jyot Singh is set to become the state's first Sikh elected official.
articles.image_caption: Georgia's political landscape is being reshaped by South Asian American candidates
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's State Senate Just Voted to Make August 15 India Independence Day
articles.excerpt: Resolution J1935 memorialises the Governor to proclaim India Independence Day in New York State — a recognition of the diaspora's political muscle in a state that is home to one of the largest Indian American communities in the Western Hemisphere.
articles.image_caption: The New York State Capitol building in Albany
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Convened All Eight US Consulates in New York. The Agenda Was the Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: India's External Affairs Minister chaired a rare all-consulates conference in New York on Saturday, reviewing bilateral ties across nine diplomatic posts — from Atlanta to Seattle — with diaspora support front and centre.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who chaired the all-consulates conference in New York
articles.nri_angle: The conference signals India's deepening investment in its US diplomatic infrastructure specifically to serve its nearly four million-strong diaspora — from consular services and trade portals to political outreach and community safety.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 85 Per Cent of Indian Households Have No Will. For NRIs, the Fallout Is Worse.
articles.excerpt: A new study exposes India's estate planning vacuum just as the country enters its largest-ever intergenerational wealth transfer — and NRIs with assets in two jurisdictions are walking into a legal minefield.
articles.image_caption: A multigenerational Indian family outdoors — the wealth they build together rarely survives the generation that earned it without a will
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with property and financial assets in both India and their country of residence face the worst consequences of India's will-making deficit — cross-border probate, FEMA complications, frozen NRO accounts, and family disputes that span continents and legal systems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Money Is Trying to Leave. The RBI Wants to Know Why.
articles.excerpt: India doubled NRI equity limits and scrapped bond taxes to lure foreign capital in. At the same time, the RBI and SEBI are sending formal queries to firms routing money out. For 31 million overseas Indians, the contradiction is personal.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins representing the currency under pressure from capital outflows
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who maintain financial lives across borders — LRS remittances, NRE/NRO accounts, offshore investments, property in India — are caught between India's simultaneous push to attract foreign capital and its heightened scrutiny of outward flows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nirav Shah Could Become the Third Indian American Governor. Maine Votes on Tuesday.
articles.excerpt: The former Maine CDC director and Biden-era federal health official is a frontrunner in a five-way Democratic primary. If he wins, he would be the first Indian American Democrat elected governor — and the first to do it in the Northeast.
articles.image_caption: A ballot being cast in a US election — Maine's primary on Tuesday could make history for Indian Americans
articles.nri_angle: Shah's candidacy marks a new chapter in Indian American political participation — moving from a donor class to a candidate class. Unlike predecessors Jindal and Haley, he is a Democrat running in a Northern state on competence rather than ideology, reflecting the community's geographic and political diversification.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Restaurant Empires Are Crossing Borders. The Target Is Not Expats — It Is Everyone.
articles.excerpt: From Sanjeev Kapoor's Yellow Chilli in Silicon Valley to Dishoom eyeing Manhattan and Bulbul opening in London, a wave of Indian restaurant chains is betting that Indian cuisine can go genuinely mainstream.
articles.image_caption: Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor, whose Yellow Chilli chain is opening its first US location in Santa Clara
articles.nri_angle: Indian cuisine abroad has long been shaped by diaspora-run independents — the corner curry houses, the family-owned dosa joints, the biryani spots that serve as cultural anchors for NRI communities. The new wave of branded Indian restaurant chains entering the US, UK, and Gulf markets represents a shift from community comfort food to global mainstream ambition, powered by diaspora demand but no longer limited to it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 17-Year-Old in Ontario Found the Flaw That Medical Science Missed for 53 Years. The Fix Fits in a Formula.
articles.excerpt: Gurnoor Kaur's EigenPulse corrects a mathematical error in pulse oximeters that has been misreading oxygen levels in darker-skinned patients since the 1970s. She is 17.
articles.image_caption: A pulse oximeter measuring blood oxygen levels on a patient's finger
articles.nri_angle: A Punjab-origin student in Canada solved a medical device flaw that disproportionately harms patients with darker skin — a problem the global medical establishment had accepted as intractable for decades. Her story illustrates how diaspora youth, straddling multiple worlds, bring perspectives that established institutions miss.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
